title: Connection orchestration fix and escalation debrief for intermittent hosted-api 5xx/timeouts
creator: Liam Chen
description: During an escalated customer incident on 2025-02-08 we observed recurring 5xx responses and elevated timeouts for a subset of hosted-api requests. Initial triage shows a pattern where long tail requests trigger aggressive client retries while the edge/proxy layer performs connection re-entry and KV cache compaction. The interaction between continuous-batching backpressure, synchronous KV compaction, and the proxy connection admission caused connection resets and retry amplification, producing high visible error rates for affected tenants. This ticket coordinates the engineering fix, rollout plan, SDK guidance, and post-incident telemetry/runbook updates so future escalations can be resolved faster and with less customer impact.
resolution_plan: Patch runtime to make KV compaction async and non-blocking for active request streams
Introduce soft admission control on the edge that returns 429 with Retry-After for overloaded connection pools instead of resetting sockets
Add per-tenant retry-hysteresis circuit in the reverse proxy that enforces exponential backoff hints to SDKs
Deploy staged canary to 10% of traffic -> 50% -> 100% with monitoring gates
Update SDK docs to prefer idempotency tokens and recommend jittered exponential backoff settings
Augment telemetry: per-tenant inflight-connection counters, compaction-duration histograms, and retry-chain traces
acceptance_criteria: No increase in host-level socket resets observed during KV compaction window in canary cluster
Customer-visible 5xx rate reduced to baseline for test tenants over 72h post rollout
New telemetry surfaces compaction latency and client retry chains in Grafana dashboards
Runbook updated with playbooks for rapid circuit activation, customer comms template, and SDK guidance
Patch merged and released in runtime-1.21 and smoke-tested against staging traffic patterns

Initial mitigation: paused compaction for 10 minutes, error rate dropped. Escalated to on-call backend and SRE.

2025-02-08 11:20 - Maya Patel (SRE): Deployed temporary slow-path that rejects new streaming handshakes for degraded hosts. Helped stabilize customer-facing traffic. Filed follow-up to avoid socket-level resets and introduce graceful degradation.

2025-02-09 08:45 - Liam Chen: Prototype patch: move kvcache compaction to background worker with cooperative yielding. Local perf tests show compaction latency reduced by 60% under load. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/23841

2025-02-10 14:12 - Aisha Kapoor: Edge admission change drafted. Instead of aborting connections, emit 429 with Retry-After backed by per-tenant queue metrics. PR for proxy: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/1129

2025-02-14 10:02 - Aisha Kapoor: Canary 10% started in us-west-2. Observability notes: compaction-duration histogram now present, retry-chain traces forwarded to X-Ray. No abnormal 5xx increase after 6 hours. Monitoring alert thresholds adjusted.
2025-02-16 18:20 - Liam Chen: After 48h in 50% canary, metrics are stable. Preparing rollout plan and SDK docs update. SDK guidance PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/pull/457

notes: Trade-offs considered: aggressive backpressure at edge reduces immediate 5xxs but increases client-side retry latency; chosen approach uses 429/Retry-After plus SDK guidance to minimize customer impact.
Rollout plan constrained by Dedicated customers who require version pinning; will coordinate with Account Ops to schedule Dedicated upgrades outside business hours.
Follow-ups: add synthetic regression tests (ENG-512409), update Dedicated deployment docs for non-blocking compaction, and add a post-release validation runbook step.
